messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Deployment mode & migration follow-up — Lumina Labs

Hi Rajiv / Emily,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to meet the Lumina team. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment on the migration and deployment mode decision (hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem).

Notes from our discussion:
- Current: self-hosted inference on legacy GPU cluster (custom wrappers around k8s + SLURM).
- Requirements: US-only data residency, SOC 2 & audit evidence, low-latency inference for chat product (p95 latency target ~120ms), peak throughput ~10 qps with bursts to 25 qps, nightly batch scoring jobs.
- Pain points: ops overhead, model updates slow, inconsistent latency during scale events.

Our initial recommendation based on above:
1) Short term (prototype): Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) to provide predictable throughput and reduce ops work while you validate migration runs.
2) Long term (prod): Private VPC or on-prem (we can support both) to meet strict data residency and compliance requirements, and integrate with your KMS/HSM.

Action items / next steps:
- Rajiv / Emily: confirm current cluster specs (GPU type, node count, network bandwidth) + attach current architecture PDF (you mentioned you would share).
- Redwood (Neha / Dev): share SOC 2 summary and a high-level migration runbook.
- Schedule a 90-minute migration workshop with engineering to map integration points (KV cache, model weights transfer, routing/fallback).

I attached a short checklist of items we typically need for the migration planning. If you want, we can run a short perf benchmark on a mirrored dataset in Dedicated to surface runtime/quantization choices before committing to Private.

Propose workshop time slots: Thu 11/12 9:30-11:00 PT or Fri 11/13 11:00-12:30 PT — which works for your eng team?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Thanks Marissa — really useful recap. Attaching our current architecture diagram (Lumina-current-architecture.pdf) as requested. Few clarifications and answers to your questions: 

- Cluster: On-prem cluster, mixed GPU types (8x A100 and 16x A40 across two racks). Scheduler: custom k8s + SLURM hybrid.
- Network: 25 Gbps between racks, 10 Gbps uplink to the data tier.
- Data residency: must remain in US data centers, but we can host in a dedicated VPC in us-east for now.
- Compliance: SOC 2 is mandatory, need copy of your controls and evidence points.
- Expected traffic: currently 10 qps baseline for chat, spikes to ~25 qps during peak; nightly batch scoring processes (millions of records) run on an ETL cluster.
- Latency target: p95 <= 120ms, p99 as low as possible.

We are leaning toward Private VPC for production due to compliance, but open to using Dedicated to stage the migration and run benchmarks. Timeline wise: would like a pilot in 4–6 weeks if feasible.

Thanks — attaching the architecture doc. Happy to confirm a workshop on Thu 11/12 9:30 PT — Emily will coordinate.

-Rajiv
CTO, Lumina Labs
rajiv@lumina.ai

Rajiv — thanks for the details and the architecture doc, very helpful.

Given the constraints (SOC 2 + US-only + latency), the phased approach still looks like the lowest-risk path:
- Phase 0: Discovery & benchmark in Redwood Dedicated (we'll mirror a small subset of traffic and dataset to validate latency and quantization configurations).
- Phase 1: Pilot in Dedicated with routing and canary for a small % of production traffic.
- Phase 2: Move to Private VPC (customer-managed VPC in us-east) for production with your KMS integration and audit log retention.

Estimate for pilot: 4–6 weeks to get Dedicated pilot running (benchmarks + canary) assuming we get access to a representative dataset and service account access for deployment. Private VPC cutover can follow in 6–8 weeks after pilot depending on network and security review.

I've attached a short SOC 2 summary for Redwood (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf) and a draft migration runbook (migration-runbook-draft.docx) — Dev, tagging you for any technical corrections.

For the workshop on Thu 11/12 9:30 PT we will review: data transfer approach, model artifact transfer, KV/prefix caching strategy, routing and fallback, metrics to validate during canary, and checklist for SOC2 evidence. Please add any agenda items you want.

If that timeline looks ok, I can get the contract/commit proposal for Dedicated started so we have capacity reserved during the pilot window.

Best,
Marissa

Quick technical notes from my side prior to the workshop:

- Integration points:
  * Inference routing: we can route by latency SLO to Dedicated for the pilot, then shift routing rules to Private for prod.
  * KV / prefix caching: plan to mirror your current KV cache keys; we'll need a migration mapping and TTL policy.
  * Model weights: we support rsync over secure tunnel for weight transfer; recommend validating checksums as part of the runbook.
- Resource assumptions for pilot: 2x A100 equivalent gpus for headroom (simulate 10–25 qps), 8–16 workers depending on batch strategy.
- Networking: recommend testing with a 10 Gbps link to avoid inter-node throttling for heavy batch jobs; we can run a synthetic traffic test during pilot.
- Security: we can integrate with your KMS (AWS KMS/HSM) and provide audit logs to your SIEM via secure syslog or S3 bucket pulls.
- Rough timeline: kickoff + infra provisioning (1 week), perf benchmark & tuning (2 weeks), canary run (1–2 weeks) — overall 4–6 weeks for pilot.

Attaching a draft migration-runbook-draft.docx to this thread for review (contains checklist and checkpoints for each phase). Please review the runbook before the workshop and highlight any gaps.

- Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
